problem_type: Canvas placement point diverges from the user-chosen screen point
symptom: User report 2026-09-21: dropping an image/video onto the generation canvas lands offset from where the mouse was released, sometimes outside the viewport (only findable via the minimap).
direct_cause: handleCanvasStageDrop hand-computed the canvas point from the stage rect plus viewport offset/zoom, pinned the node's top-left corner to the cursor, clamped x/y to >= 40, and OS/workspace drops went through addNode collision avoidance.
class_root: A pre-React-Flow invariant (canvas coordinates are non-negative, clamp to >= 40) survived the kernel migration in three placement writers, and screen-to-canvas conversion was re-implemented outside the kernel. With the viewport in negative coordinates every drop/paste at the cursor is pushed right/down, possibly off-screen.
affected_population: Every user who panned the generation canvas left/up of the origin and then drops OS files, project-tree files, asset-library cards or browser asset-box items, or pastes at the cursor
entry_points: Stage drop (OS files / project tree / asset library / browser asset box)
Import layout for toolbar and context-menu import

external_sources.purpose: React Flow places a node created at a drop point via screenToFlowPosition({x: clientX, y: clientY}) with an origin anchor on the node; negative flow coordinates are valid (installed @xyflow/react 12.11.5).

invariants: Screen-to-canvas conversion for drops comes only from the kernel (flow.screenToFlowPosition), passed in as CanvasStageDropContext.toCanvasPoint.
No placement writer clamps canvas coordinates to a positive floor; negative coordinates are preserved.

A drop places the first card with the cursor at its anchor (grab point for asset-library cards, visible-card center otherwise; OS images are anchored on their real pixel-ratio card size inside the import adapter) and does not run collision avoidance.

door_reduction.why_not: The doors are distinct drag sources (browser asset box, asset library, project tree, OS files), import callers (toolbar, context menu, asset library panel, effects) and paste shortcuts; they already converge on handleCanvasStageDrop, layoutImportPositions and pasteNodes, which are the boundaries fixed here.

generality_proof: All four drop sources derive their origin from the single resolveDropOrigin(ctx.toCanvasPoint(...)) inside handleCanvasStageDrop, and the only remaining positive-floor clamps (canvasStageDrop layout, assetImportAdapter layout, pasteNodes) are deleted, so no caller can reintroduce the offset through these boundaries.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Owns the drop point: kernel conversion via toCanvasPoint, anchor via resolveDropOrigin, exact placement for every drop source.
Lays imported files out from the given origin without clamping.
Pastes at the requested canvas point without clamping.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Now passes getCanvasPointFromClientPoint (flow.screenToFlowPosition) as toCanvasPoint; the offset/zoom fields no longer exist on CanvasStageDropContext, so hand math cannot compile.
Same Math.max(40) clamp found by rg 'Math.max(40' src/workbench; removed; regression test pastes at (-800,-300).
Uses Math.round(basePosition) without a floor clamp; its basePosition comes from the shortcut paste position already converted by the kernel.

recurrence.reason: Any user whose viewport sits in negative canvas coordinates hits it on every drop or cursor paste; four drag sources and the paste path share the mechanism.
same_class_scan: rg 'Math.max(40' src/workbench: canvasStageDrop.ts, assetImportAdapter.ts, generationCanvasStore.ts (all removed)
rg 'screenToFlowPosition|getBoundingClientRect' src/workbench/generationCanvas: context menu, frame tool and paste already use the kernel; stage drop was the only hand-rolled conversion

prevention.invariant: Drop placement = kernel-converted cursor point minus the card anchor, unclamped, exact.
prevention.failure_mode: A caller that tries to pass viewport offset/zoom fails typecheck because CanvasStageDropContext only accepts toCanvasPoint.
prevention.strategy: Replace the hand-rolled conversion with a required kernel converter in the context type, route every drop source through resolveDropOrigin, and delete all positive-floor clamps in placement writers.

legacy_paths.rationale: clampNodePos, the offset/zoom hand conversion, resolveAssetLibraryDropPosition and both inline Math.max(40) clamps are deleted in the same change.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: @xyflow/react 12.11.5 already provides screenToFlowPosition and negative coordinates; the defect was our code bypassing it.

migration: No data migration: existing node positions are untouched; only new placements change. Nodes previously clamped to 40 stay where they are.
residual_risks: Video cards are anchored on the default 340x280 card because the aspect is unknown until metadata loads; the card then shrinks with its top edge fixed (real-app walkthrough: center moves up 44 px on 16:9, release point stays inside the card).
Project-tree/browser/asset-library image drops anchor on the default card size; the cursor stays inside the card but may be off-center.
Native OS drag cannot be automated; tests/ux/canvas-drop-at-cursor.walk.mjs dispatches a DOM drop with a real disk-backed File (zh-CN and en pass; old code fails 10 checks).

invariant_owner_layer.why: 「落点=松手点」由 canvasStageDrop.ts 单点持有：屏幕→画布换算只经 CanvasStageDropContext.toCanvasPoint（内核提供，类型上不再有 offset/zoom 可手算），锚点只经 resolveDropOrigin；两个下游布局（layoutImportPositions / pasteNodes）只负责不钳制。两份测试都做过阳性对照：把 ≥40 钳制放回去即红。
